subject: Marketplace price tilt & reseller uplift playbook
body:
Message 1
----------
From: Aisha Khan <aisha@northstarlabs.com>
To: priyom_das@redwood.com, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 5 Oct 2026 08:42:00 -0700
Subject: Marketplace packaging + reseller uplift question

Hi Priyom / Stephanie,

We're preparing our procurement request for a private offer on AWS Marketplace and want to understand a couple of things from Redwood:
- How should we present list price vs customer discount so our reseller (ValueTech Partners) still sees a healthy margin?
- Can we keep the marketplace listing price intact (for comparability) and provide a separate reseller uplift/credit?
- Any recommended invoice routing or line-item structure that keeps marketplace reporting clean while honoring reseller economics?

We've attached our RFP and rough usage profile (Northstar_RFP_202610.pdf). Our procurement deadline is Oct 22; earliest go-live desired Nov 1.

Thanks — Aisha
Aisha Khan
Head of Cloud Procurement, Northstar Labs

Message 2
----------
From: PrIyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Khan <aisha@northstarlabs.com>
Cc: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 5 Oct 2026 10:15:32 -0700
Subject: Re: Marketplace packaging + reseller uplift question

Hi Aisha — thanks for the clear brief. Quick summary of an approach that balances marketplace comparability and reseller economics:

1) Keep the public listing price stable (don’t change published SKU price).
2) Offer a private-offer price that is structured as: committed-usage bands + a line-item "Customer Discount" applied in the private-offer (not a listing change).
3) Provide reseller uplift as a separate passthrough credit on the invoice ("Reseller Partner Credit") rather than embedding into the private-offer list price. This preserves marketplace metrics while making the uplift visible to your reseller.
4) If tax/finance requires, include a reconciliation line on the invoice referencing the private offer id.

I attached a working packaging matrix (NSL_PrivateOffer_Packaging_v1.xlsx) with three banded commit tiers and two uplift options (pass-through credit vs. pre-funded partner fee). High-level pros/cons included in the sheet.

Next steps I propose:
- Stephanie to propose commission tranching and tax treatment.
- Jonas to confirm ops/invoice mapping for AWS Marketplace listing.
- We’ll iterate and produce final PO template for DocuSign.

Happy to hop on a short call if you prefer.

Best,
Priyom
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference

Attachments: NSL_PrivateOffer_Packaging_v1.xlsx (attachment stub)

Message 3

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 6 Oct 2026 09:20:05 -0700
Subject: Re: Marketplace packaging + reseller uplift question

Thanks Priyom — added a couple of practical notes from finance/legal: 
- Preferred pattern is 1) base commission (paid to reseller monthly), 2) success fee (paid after onboarding milestones). Example: 7% base + 3% success fee tied to first 90 days.
- For AWS Marketplace, we recommend the uplift be recorded as a credit line on Redwood's invoice to Northstar and separately reimbursed to the reseller via Redwood payout (keeps AWS metering/reporting clean).
- If Northstar prefers, we can set the uplift as a short-term concession (e.g., 12 months) rather than a permanent discount; this avoids distorting public list comparables.

I exported a simple commission table (commission-table.csv) — shows the banding and sample calculations.

Cc'ing Jonas to confirm mapping to listing SKU and invoice fields.

-Steph
Director, Revenue Operations

Attachments: commission-table.csv (attachment stub)

Message 4
----------
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, PrIyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Aisha Khan <aisha@northstarlabs.com>
Date: Thu, 8 Oct 2026 14:40:18 -0700
Subject: Re: Marketplace packaging + reseller uplift question

A couple of ops things to flag:
- AWS metering ties refunds/credits to the private-offer id. If we put the reseller uplift as a credit, we must ensure the private-offer id is present in the invoice and reconciliation flow; otherwise AWS reporting will mismatch.
- Invoice routing: for pass-through credits, we need to set Redwood as the seller-of-record and include a separate PO line for the "Reseller Partner Credit" with a negative amount. Some finance teams prefer the reseller to invoice separately to avoid negative line items — both are possible, we should pick what Northstar procurement prefers.
- HubSpot mapping: mark deal stage to "Contracting (Marketplace)" and add a task for legal to review carveouts for channel visibility.

One behavioral recommendation: use a time-bound uplift (6-12 months) with documented reconciliation — keeps long-term list pricing clean while honoring channel economics.

-Jonas
Director, Deal Operations

Message 5
----------
From: PrIyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Khan <aisha@northstarlabs.com>
Cc: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com, legal@redwood.com, finance@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 9 Oct 2026 11:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Marketplace packaging + reseller uplift question

Aisha — thanks for the patience. Attached is an updated packaging workbook (NSL_PrivateOffer_Packaging_v3.xlsx) and a PO template we usually send to marketplace customers (Approved-PO-Template.pdf). Summary of decisions we recommend for Northstar:
- Private-offer with committed bands, public listing price unchanged.
- Reseller uplift handled as a pass-through credit line on Redwood invoice; term = 12 months.
- Commission: 7% base + 3% success fee, payable per agreed schedule in commission-table.csv.
- Ops: include private-offer id on invoice; Redwood finance will reconcile monthly and provide a partner payout report.

Requested asks from Northstar to finalize:
1) Confirm you want the reseller credit as a Redwood-issued negative line item on the invoice, or whether ValueTech should invoice Northstar directly.
2) Confirm procurement timeline (you had Oct 22 as the deadline).

If that sounds good I'll loop legal to draft the private-offer terms and produce a DocuSign-ready package.

Best,
Priyom

Attachments: NSL_PrivateOffer_Packaging_v3.xlsx, Approved-PO-Template.pdf

Thanks — this is helpful and aligns with what ValueTech expects. We prefer Redwood to issue the reseller credit as a negative invoice line (ValueTech has asked to avoid additional invoicing steps on our side).

Procurement timeline: we’ll be ready to sign Nov 1, assuming legal review completes by Oct 26. Please send the DocuSign package and final PO template when available.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

—Aisha
